summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest UK/EU movers.

• 6 upside misses — REN.AS +5%, CA.PA +4%, STLAP.PA +4%, BEI.DE +4%, FME.DE +3%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (BESI.AS -6%, FRES.L -5%, ANTO.L -5%, AAF.L -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: BESI.AS (-6.30%) — Dutch media reported Samsung/SK Hynix are weighing delaying hybrid-bonding adoption (favoring a new heat-dissipation approach instead), undercutting BESI's core long-term growth driver. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe — BESI.AS is a mid/large-cap Euronext Amsterdam semiconductor-equipment name not covered by the bot's tradable universe, likely filtered out by exchange/sector scope rather than a technical signal.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day headline; closest driver found is a recent Citi upgrade to Buy on RELX, plus an active £100m share buyback tranche running through July — no single hard catalyst identified for 2026-07-07.
top_movers.miss_reason: REN.AS is RELX's secondary Euronext Amsterdam listing (primary line is LSE: REL.L); a UK/EU strategy universe built around primary listings would exclude this thinly-traded dual-listed line entirely, so it was never in scope.
top_movers.suggestion: Add cross-listing consolidation: map dual-listed tickers (e.g. REN.AS) to their primary line's universe membership so large-cap names aren't dropped just because the secondary listing isn't separately whitelisted.

top_movers.catalyst: RBC initiated coverage 7/7/26 with Outperform and €22 target (~33% upside), naming Carrefour its top European food-retail pick.
top_movers.miss_reason: CA.PA sits outside any active strategy's universe (foreign large-cap grocery retailer, Euronext Paris listing, not a US/ADR name) — the move is an analyst-initiation re-rating, not a technical or volume signal a domestic momentum/mean-reversion bot would ever see.
top_movers.suggestion: If EU retail exposure is desired, add a screened uk-eu large-cap universe (CAC40/Euro Stoxx constituents) with an analyst-initiation event feed trigger, rather than trying to catch this via US-centric technical filters.

top_movers.catalyst: Stellantis posted strong June US sales (+10% YoY), Q2 (+6%) and H1 2026 (+5% YoY) results; stock re-rated up despite a same-week HSBC downgrade on inventory concerns.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STLAP.PA is the Paris line of dual-listed Stellantis (NYSE: STLA). The uk-eu universe likely dedups cross-listings to the US ticker, or excludes EU large-cap auto OEMs as a sector.
top_movers.suggestion: Check if STLA (NYSE) captured this move under the same name; if not, add a cross-listing map so uk-eu strategies can route dual-listed names to whichever venue (Paris vs NYSE) has the deeper liquidity/signal.

top_movers.catalyst: No clear news driver — no earnings (next report Aug 5), no M&A/analyst catalyst found; move looks like defensive-sector rotation into EU consumer staples.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BEI.DE is a DAX-listed EU consumer-staples/personal-care large-cap, a category the bot's universes (likely US-centric or momentum/tech-focused) don't currently cover.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a DAX/EuroStoxx consumer-staples sleeve (or broaden uk-eu universe filters to include large-cap defensive names) so unhedged EU rotation moves like this register as candidates.

top_movers.catalyst: No single fundamental catalyst — steady €600M buyback (609,595 shares, ~€24M bought back June29-Jul3) pushed shares to a 13-week high; JPMorgan even cut to Underweight same day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — FME.DE is a German dual-listed (NYSE: FMS) dialysis/medtech name; uk-eu universes likely exclude healthcare tickers carrying pending regulatory event risk (e.g. TAVNEOS EU authorization loss) rather than pure momentum names.
top_movers.suggestion: Add DAX large-cap healthcare/medtech (mkt cap >€20B) to the uk-eu universe, or add a corporate-buyback-flow signal (disclosed weekly repurchase volume vs ADV) so sustained company-driven buying triggers inclusion, not just news-gap screens.

top_movers.catalyst: No single confirmed news item; shares extended a multi-day rally (+2.23% Jul 6, +3.11% Jul 7) amid favorable FCA rule changes (mortgage lending reforms, new targeted-support advice regime) lifting UK wealth managers ahead of Jul 29 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — STJ.L is a UK LSE-listed diversified-financials/wealth-management name; bot's coverage likely skews to US large-cap/momentum names and doesn't track FTSE-listed financial advisers or UK regulatory-driven sector rotations.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a UK diversified-financials/wealth-manager watchlist (FTSE350 constituents) with an FCA-regulatory-catalyst tag so sector-wide rallies tied to advice/mortgage rule changes are picked up pre-earnings.

top_movers.catalyst: Dutch media reported Samsung/SK Hynix are weighing delaying hybrid-bonding adoption (favoring a new heat-dissipation approach instead), undercutting BESI's core long-term growth driver.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — BESI.AS is a mid/large-cap Euronext Amsterdam semiconductor-equipment name not covered by the bot's tradable universe, likely filtered out by exchange/sector scope rather than a technical signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add Euronext Amsterdam large-cap semi-equipment names (BESI.AS) to universe with a news-gate rule that flags supply-chain-partner headlines (Samsung/SK Hynix roadmap news) mentioning a name's core product line.

top_movers.catalyst: No firm-specific news; move tracks a broad pullback in silver/gold (silver ~$61.5/oz, -1.4%+ on USD strength) after last week's rally to record highs.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — FRES.L is a Mexico-domiciled, GBP-listed precious-metals miner; likely excluded by a sector/commodity-beta filter that keeps materials/mining names (high correlation to spot silver/gold rather than idiosyncratic drivers) out of equity universes.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a narrow commodity-miner bucket (silver/gold >X% metal-price beta) to the uk-eu universe so names like FRES.L become eligible when spot silver/gold moves >2% in a session.

top_movers.catalyst: Trump threatened a 50% US tariff on copper imports, spiking COMEX copper ~13% and dragging LSE-listed copper miners (Antofagasta, Anglo American, Glencore) down 3%+ in sympathy despite global copper prices only easing modestly.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — ANTO.L is a Chile-focused, London-listed large-cap copper miner, a foreign/commodity-sector name likely excluded from US-equity-centric universes. Also a macro/policy-driven sector move (tariff headline), not a stock-specific signal a single-name news scanner would flag.
top_movers.suggestion: Add LSE metals & mining large-caps (e.g. FTSE 350 mining subsector) to universe, and add a commodity-policy headline trigger (tariff/export-control news on key metals) that maps to sector-wide short-term exposure across foreign miners/producers.

top_movers.catalyst: No single same-day headline found; likely renewed investor concern over the Jul 31 Airtel Money IPO deadline and $515M buyback liability if the listing slips again.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe — AAF.L is a frontier-market (African telecom) LSE listing with USD-denominated earnings/dividends, a category typically excluded from developed-market uk-eu screens on cap/liquidity or FX-risk grounds.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a frontier/EM-Africa telecom bucket (LSE-listed, mkt cap >£10B) to the uk-eu universe with an event flag for pending subsidiary-IPO/buyback-liability deadlines so contingent-liability-driven drawdowns are catchable.
